newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan media hail HK handover, wary about future.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan media hail HK handover, wary about future.

text.p: Taipei media commentators on Monday hailed Hong Kong's imminent absorption by Taiwan's rival China, but said the island should keep a wary eye on future ties with Hong Kong and Beijing.

Major newspapers gave prominent coverage to Hong Kong's midnight return to communist China, with state and private electronic media planning extensive live broadcasts as the British colony undergoes its historic handover.

"Hong Kong's handover symbolises the end of humiliation of the Chinese nation dating to the mid 19th century and the start of a new era in Asia and the world," the Commercial Times, one of the island's top business dailies, said in an editorial.
In a commentary titled "The Complete Termination of The Colonial Era", the mass circulation China Times said: "Hong Kong's return is a major event in Chinese history."

"The Chinese people are able to declare to the world that they have 'stood up'," it said, echoing words used by Mao Zedong when he proclaimed the communist People's Republic that unseated the Republic of China, now in exile on Taiwan.
"What's more, the Chinese people need to demonstrate to the entire world that they can rule Hong Kong and make Hong Kong a even better place."
But commentators cautioned that Hong Kong's shift toward Beijing did not guarantee better Taipei-Beijing ties.

"The drastically different political and economic systems in Hong Kong and the mainland and special conditions among Taiwan, Hong Kong and the mainland bring unprecedented challenges for the three places," the Commercial Times said.

Beijing, which has viewed Taiwan as a rebel-held province since a 1949 civil war split, says the return of Hong Kong, and Portuguese-run Macau in 1999, will leave Taiwan as the only territory still awaiting "reunification with the motherland".
A confident China says its implementation of Hong Kong's highly autonomous "one country, two systems" experience should reassure Taiwan of its own future under mainland sovereignty.
Under the system agreed by Britain and China in 1984, Hong Kong can maintain its capitalist systems for 50 years after it reverts to Beijing.
Another leading business newspaper, the Economic Daily News, said whether Beijing can live up to its promises to Hong Kong remained to be seen.
"Maintaining close economic and trade contacts between Taiwan and Hong Kong is most desirable for the three places," the Economic Daily News said.
"It's worth paying attention to whether Beijing authorities can live up to its promise to Hong Kong..., whether Beijing will use Hong Kong as a tool to deal with Taiwan," it said.
Hong Kong is an important transit point for more than $30 billion in investment that has poured into China from Taiwan since the easing of unofficial ties in the late 1980s.

"What Taiwan should do after Hong Kong's handover to the mainland is make itself an economically prosperous, politically stable society, and continue negotiations and intercourse with the mainland," the English-language China Post said.

"Here is a word of advice to rulers in Beijing: You should be careful about the way you rule post-1997 Hong Kong and how you treat the Hong Kongers. Your handling of the region and its people will be a major factor in how the people of Taiwan view the reunification issue," it said.
